title: The Long Game: Why AI Implementation Is a Rebuild, Not a Rollout
author: Nick Potkalitsky
summary: Reporting from a presentation to the Ohio 8 Coalition of large urban school districts facing a legislative deadline to adopt an AI policy by July 2026, Nick Potkalitsky argues that genuine AI implementation is a three-to-five-year rebuild, not a quick rollout, and that anyone offering easy solutions has not grasped the complexity. He treats the policy deadline as an opportunity to build comprehensive guidance rather than check a box, and lays out four foundational shifts: instructional redesign that assumes any out-of-class work is done with AI, assessment redesign to address the crisis of teachers not knowing what students know, purposive technology ecosystems chosen by discernment over accumulation, and teacher-led curriculum rebuilding that pairs top-down training with bottom-up cohorts. Citing data on student emotional dependence and disconnection, he insists the answer is not less AI but more intentional implementation, centered on teachers and the most vulnerable students.
points: Potkalitsky's central message is that AI implementation is a 3-5 year rebuild, and anyone offering easy solutions has not grasped the full complexity.
Instructional redesign should start from the premise that any work sent outside of class will be completed with the assistance of AI.
Assessment is in crisis because many teachers no longer know what students know, requiring either robust AI systems or serious process pedagogy.
Districts should choose technology by discernment of purpose rather than accumulating every AI-powered tool, tied to what student data they need to see.
Teachers remain the superpower of this disruption, so top-down PD must be complemented by teacher cohorts rebuilding curriculum from the ground up.
quotes: We are in the middle of a 3-5 year rebuild. Anyone offering easy solutions hasn’t come to grips with the full complexity of what we’re facing.
Here’s the foundational premise: Any work sent outside of class will be completed with the assistance of AI.
We are in a crisis moment. Many teachers simply do not know what students know anymore.
The solution isn’t less AI. It’s more intentional implementation.
teachers will continue to be the drivers of change over the next 5-10 years.
If your AI plan doesn’t explicitly address students with IEPs, students in poverty, and students already disconnected, it’s not a plan—it’s a hope.
